title: Reed pens in ancient Egypt
text: Scribes cut reeds to a point and wrote with carbon-based ink on papyrus. The reed pen became the basic writing tool of the ancient world.

title: The quill takes over
text: Feather quills, cut and shaped to hold more ink, became the main pen in Europe for about a thousand years.

title: A pen with an ink reservoir in Egypt
text: Accounts say the caliph al-Mu'izz asked for a pen that would not stain his hands, and a pen with an ink reservoir was made for him.

title: Two quills, one reservoir
text: The German Daniel Schwenter described a pen made from two quills, with one holding ink to feed the other.

title: Steel nibs go into mass production
text: Birmingham makers turned out steel nibs by the million, making writing cheap, though they still needed a dip into the inkwell.

title: Poenaru patents a fountain pen
text: The Romanian Petrache Poenaru received a French patent for a pen with a quill barrel that held ink and a nib that wrote continuously.

title: Waterman patents a reliable feed
text: Lewis Waterman's feed carried ink to the nib at a steady rate, solving the blobs and dry spells that plagued earlier fountain pens.

title: George Parker starts his company
text: Parker began in Janesville, Wisconsin, and became one of the great names in pens.

title: The crescent filler
text: Conklin introduced a self-filling system: press the crescent ring on the barrel to squeeze the sac inside.

title: Onoto's plunger filler
text: The British Onoto brought the plunger filler to market, drawing ink into the barrel with a syringe-like action.

title: Simplo Filler Pen Company
text: The firm that would become Montblanc began in Hamburg. The Montblanc name followed in 1910.

title: Luxmy Stylo Pen Works in Varanasi
text: Dr R. N. Saha set up one of the early Indian pen works. One history of Indian pens dates it to 1907.

title: Sheaffer's lever filler
text: Walter Sheaffer patented a side lever that squeezed the sac, making self-filling pens practical for everyone.

title: The button filler and Sheaffer
text: Sheaffer started its own company in 1913, and Parker adopted a button filler around the same time.

title: Deccan Pen Stores opens in Hyderabad
text: S. A. Siddiqui started as a shop and repair business and later made his own pens.

title: Parker Duofold
text: A big red-barrelled pen that made pens a fashion item as well as a tool.

title: Montblanc Meisterstück
text: The Meisterstück line began and became a hallmark of luxury pens.

title: First Pelikan piston filler
text: Pelikan launched its first piston-filler pen, based on a patent by Theodor Kovács. The Sheaffer Balance also arrived this year.

title: Parker Vacumatic
text: A striped, translucent barrel and a vacuum diaphragm filler let you see how much ink was left.

title: Ratnam Pen Works, Rajahmundry
text: Two brothers began making ebonite pens. Gandhi rejected their first as not swadeshi enough, then thanked them for a second pen in 1935.

title: The ballpoint is patented
text: The Hungarian László Bíró patented a ballpoint pen that would eventually take over everyday writing.

title: Parker 51
text: One of the most popular pens ever, with a hooded nib and quick-drying ink.

title: Chelpark takes over Parker's Indian arm
text: The Chellaram family, with Parker, took over Parker's Indian subsidiary. It later made its own pens and ink in Bangalore.

title: Aurora 88
text: Marcello Nizzoli's streamlined Italian pen, a mid-century classic.

title: Aerometric filler
text: Parker introduced the Aerometric: a squeezable sac in a metal sleeve, used on the 51.

title: Snorkel and the Meisterstück 149
text: Sheaffer's Snorkel let you fill without dipping the nib, and Montblanc launched the 149 and 146.

title: Pilot Pen Company (India) is formed
text: The Indian arm of Pilot was incorporated in 1952, while makers such as Hilal started brands like Sultan the same year.

title: The first cartridge pen
text: Waterman brought out the C/F, built around a plastic ink cartridge, making refilling clean for the first time.

title: Parker 61 and capillary filling
text: The Parker 61 filled by capillary action: you simply dip the nib and ink is drawn in.

title: Pilot Capless
text: Pilot launched a pen with a retractable nib, no cap needed.

title: Lamy 2000
text: Gerd A. Müller's Bauhaus-inspired pen, still in production with barely any change.

title: India reserves fountain pens for small makers
text: Fountain pens became a small-scale industry product, which shaped who could make them for decades.

title: Lamy Safari
text: A bright, affordable school pen that introduced millions of people to fountain pens.

title: A new wave of makers
text: With the internet bringing collectors and makers together, Japanese, Chinese and Taiwanese makers found new audiences and fountain pens enjoyed a revival.

title: India lifts import limits on fountain pens
text: Import restrictions were removed only in April 2001, after which foreign pens became easier to buy.

title: TWSBI ECO
text: An affordable clear piston-filler that opened piston pens to beginners.
